# futures::Poll - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/futures/0.1.31/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/futures/type.Poll.html

Return type of the `Future::poll` method, indicates whether a future’s value
is ready or not.

- `Ok(Async::Ready(t))`means that a future has successfully resolved
- `Ok(Async::NotReady)`means that a future is not ready to complete yet
- `Err(e)`means that a future has completed with the given failure

---

# futures::StartSend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/futures/0.1.31/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/futures/type.StartSend.html

Return type of the `Sink::start_send` method, indicating the outcome of a
send attempt. See `AsyncSink` for more details.

---

# re_viewer_context - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/re_viewer_context/0.34.0-rc.4/re_viewer_context/

## Expand description

Rerun Viewer context

This crate contains data structures that are shared with most modules of the viewer.

- Receiver for the `CommandSender`

# re_renderer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/re_renderer/0.34.0-rc.4/re_renderer/

## Expand description

Rerun’s renderer.

A wgpu based renderer [wgpu](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/) for all your visualization needs.
Used in `re_runner` to display the contents of any view contents other than pure UI.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

- `import-dae`- *(enabled by default)*— Support importing .dae files
- `import-gltf`- *(enabled by default)*— Support importing .gltf and .glb files
- `import-obj`- *(enabled by default)*— Support importing .obj files
- `import-stl`- *(enabled by default)*— Support importing binary & ascii .stl files

[§](https://docs.rs#draw-recording-overview)Draw recording overview

[ ViewBuilder](https://docs.rs/view_builder/struct.ViewBuilder.html) are the main entry point for all draw operations.
Each

[represents a rectangular screen area that is composited into the target surface via](https://docs.rs/view_builder/struct.ViewBuilder.html)

`ViewBuilder`[.](https://docs.rs/view_builder/struct.ViewBuilder.html#method.composite)

`ViewBuilder::composite`A user supplies [ renderer::DrawData](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.DrawData.html)s to the

[. Upon submission, the](https://docs.rs/view_builder/struct.ViewBuilder.html)

`ViewBuilder`[collects the](https://docs.rs/view_builder/struct.ViewBuilder.html)

`ViewBuilder`[s from the](https://docs.rs/struct.Drawable.html)

`Drawable`[and adds them to the appropriate work queues of each draw phase.](https://docs.rs/struct.QueueableDrawData.html)

`QueueableDrawData`[s map roughly 1:1 to wgpu draw calls and have a](https://docs.rs/struct.Drawable.html)

`Drawable`[type specific payload that identifies them within their](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.DrawData.html)

`renderer::DrawData`[.](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.DrawData.html)

`renderer::DrawData`Depending on the [ DrawPhase](https://docs.rs/enum.DrawPhase.html) sorting of drawables may occur:
for instance

[sorts far to near to facilitate blending, whereas other phases aggressively bundle by](https://docs.rs/enum.DrawPhase.html#variant.Transparent)

`DrawPhase::Transparent`[types to minimize state changes.](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.DrawData.html)

`renderer::DrawData`Each [ renderer::DrawData](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.DrawData.html) is associated with a single

[. These encapsulate the knowledge (i.e. renderpipelines etc.) of how to render a certain kind of primitive. Unlike](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.Renderer.html)

`renderer::Renderer`[s,](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.DrawData.html)

`renderer::DrawData`[s are immutable and long-lived.](https://docs.rs/renderer/trait.Renderer.html)

`renderer::Renderer`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use resource_managers::`- [AlphaChannelUsage](https://docs.rs/resource_managers/enum.AlphaChannelUsage.html);
- `pub use texture_readback::`- [TextureReadback](https://docs.rs/texture_readback/struct.TextureReadback.html);

# re_data_source - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/re_data_source/0.34.0-rc.4/re_data_source/

## Expand description

Handles different ways of loading Rerun data, e.g.:

- Over HTTPS
- Over gRPC
- From disk

Also handles different file types: rrd, images, text files, 3D models, point clouds…

- The contents of a file.

- Options for `LogDataSource::from_uri`

- Analytics data extracted from a `LogDataSource`

- Controls how a newly loaded recording is treated by the viewer.

# rill_graph - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rill-graph/0.5.0-beta.7/rill_graph/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rill-graph--static-dag-signal-graph)Rill Graph — Static DAG Signal Graph

This crate provides an immutable signal graph with static topology.
Build once with `GraphBuilder`. The graph is a pure topology description
— processing is driven by port-level methods (`pre_process`,
`snapshot_feedback`, `propagate`) called from external code.

[§](https://docs.rs#key-features)Key Features

- **Static DAG topology**— connections are fixed after build
- **Kahn’s algorithm**— automatic topological sort with cycle detection
- **Auto FanOut/FanIn**— connections classified by topology (user never chooses)
- **Port-owned routing**— downstream connections and feedback state live on ports
- **Copy-based buffer routing**— separate input/output buffer pools (zero-copy planned)
- **Safe Rust**— no- `unsafe`code

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use factory::`- [NodeConstructor](https://docs.rs/factory/trait.NodeConstructor.html);
- `pub use factory::`- [NodeFactory](https://docs.rs/factory/struct.NodeFactory.html);
- `pub use factory::`- [RegistryError](https://docs.rs/factory/enum.RegistryError.html);

- [backend_](https://docs.rs/backend_factory/index.html)- factory
- Backend factory for constructing I/O backends by name.
- [factory](https://docs.rs/factory/index.html)
- Node factory and registry for constructing nodes by type name.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Prelude for convenient imports

- Register a node constructor by type name.

- Mutable builder for an immutable signal graph.

- A named resource (tape loop) shared between nodes in the graph.
